d_firstorder.t: A supplier offers {n} a discount on a bigger first order
d_firstorder.b: Your main supplier will take 8% off if you order about {$v} worth of goods in one go. The stock has to be sold, and the cash is gone until it is.

opts.d: Cash is tied up in stock for about two months. If it sells in time you save money; if it ages on the shelf you write some off.

opts.l: Order a bit more than usual
opts.d: A smaller discount and much less risk.
No discount, no risk.

d_festival_shift.t: A festival is coming to town near {n}
d_festival_shift.b: A three-day local festival is expected to bring thousands of people past your door. Extra hands cost money and the crowd is not guaranteed.

opts.l: Hire an extra shift for the weekend
opts.d: Costs extra wages. If the crowds come, you earn it back; if the weather is bad, you do not.

opts.l: Open a stall at the festival
opts.d: A smaller outlay and a chance to reach new customers.
You still get some of the extra trade.

d_secondhand_gear.t: A used machine is offered to {n} at half price
d_secondhand_gear.b: A retiring owner is selling good second-hand equipment at about half of the new price. It looks fine, but no one can be sure how long it lasts.

opts.d: Costs money now and adds capacity. About 8 in 10 such deals work out; the rest break down early.
Nothing changes.

d_local_ad.t: The local paper and radio offer {n} an advertising package
d_local_ad.b: A salesperson offers a bundle of adverts at a discount. Local reach is real, but results vary a lot.

opts.d: About half of local campaigns pay for themselves. The other half bring little.
A small cost and a small effect.
Nothing changes.

d_trainee.t: A school offers {n} a summer trainee
d_trainee.b: A keen student can help for the summer. It takes some of your time to train them, and they leave in autumn.

opts.d: A little cost and a little time. A useful pair of hands, now and then more.
Nothing changes.

d_popup_market.t: A weekend market has a stall free for {n}
d_popup_market.b: A busy weekend market has had a cancellation. A stall costs money and a lot of effort, and brings new faces.

opts.d: Cost of the stall and the work. About 6 in 10 weekends repay it, with new regulars as a bonus.
Nothing changes.

d_friend_job.t: A friend wants a big favour from {n}
d_friend_job.b: A friend wants a large job done at cost price and promises to recommend you to everyone. These promises are often forgotten.

opts.d: You lose the margin. About 3 in 10 times it really brings new customers.

opts.l: Do it at a fair price
opts.d: Your friend may say yes, and may be upset.
Nothing changes.

d_seo_promise.t: A marketer promises {n} first place on search
d_seo_promise.b: A company says it can put you at the top of search results for a monthly fee. Most such promises disappoint.

opts.d: Costs a lot. About 2 in 10 such deals bring real new customers.
A small cost. Only 1 in 4 is worth keeping.
Nothing changes.

d_cheap_supplier.t: A new supplier undercuts the prices of {n}
d_cheap_supplier.b: A supplier you do not know offers prices 15% below your current one. The quality and reliability are unproven.

opts.d: About half the time it works and you save a lot. Otherwise quality slips, and so do customers.
A smaller saving, and much less risk.
Nothing changes.

d_extra_phone_line.t: A call centre offers to answer {n}'s phone
d_extra_phone_line.b: A service picks up calls and takes bookings when you are busy. A monthly fee applies.

opts.d: Fewer missed calls. Costs money each month.
Nothing changes.

d_lease_expand.t: The unit next to {n} is free
d_lease_expand.b: The shop next door has closed, and the landlord offers you the lease. It would let you grow, and costs {$v} for fit-out and deposit.

opts.l: Take it and fit it out
opts.d: A big spend. About 6 in 10 times demand grows to fill the space; otherwise you carry a half-empty room.
A smaller cost and steadier use of the space.
No risk, no growth.

d_rival_talks.t: A rival owner asks to talk to you about {n}
d_rival_talks.b: A competitor wants to meet. It might be a merger, a buyout of your customers, or a way of getting information about you.

opts.d: About half of such meetings lead to a real offer. Taking it means losing some customers.
Costs a lot. About 6 in 10 times you gain their customers.
Nothing changes.

d_sponsor_team.t: The local team asks {n} to sponsor the shirts
d_sponsor_team.b: A local sports club needs a main sponsor. It is visible in the town. About half of such deals bring measurable sales.

opts.d: A real cost for a year. Your name is everywhere.
A small cost and a small boost.
Nothing changes.

d_supplier_lock.t: A supplier offers {n} a fixed price for years
d_supplier_lock.b: A fixed price protects you if prices go up and costs you if they fall. Nobody knows which way they will go: it is close to even.

opts.d: Close to a coin flip. A bigger win or loss over a longer time.
A smaller bet over a shorter time.
Nothing changes.

d_premium_line.b: A higher-priced range could lift the brand and the average sale. It could also fall flat and confuse customers.

opts.d: A big cost. About 55% of the time it works well.
A modest cost and a modest effect.
Nothing changes.

d_online_orders.b: More customers now look for orders and bookings online. You can build your own, or use a platform that takes a cut.

opts.d: A real cost. About 6 in 10 times it grows sales well; otherwise only a little.
A low cost, and the platform keeps part of each sale.
Nothing changes.

d_salesperson.t: A salesperson offers to join {n} on commission
d_salesperson.b: An experienced salesperson with a contact book wants to sell for you on commission and a small base pay.

opts.d: Costs recruiting and base pay. About 6 in 10 times new contracts follow.
A little more of your time.
Nothing changes.

d_certification.t: A quality certificate would open doors for {n}
d_certification.b: Large customers prefer certified suppliers. The audit takes time and money, and can be failed on the first try.

opts.d: A real cost and some disruption. Most firms pass; some have to repeat it.
Nothing changes.

d_energy_contract.t: A fixed energy price is offered to {n}
d_energy_contract.b: An energy supplier will fix your price for two years. If prices rise you win; if they fall you pay more than the market.

opts.d: About a coin flip: no one knows where prices will go.
Nothing changes.

d_fleet_replace.b: Your vehicles are ageing. A dealer offers new ones against your trade-in. Waiting is cheap until something breaks.

opts.d: A big cost, fewer breakdowns and lower running costs.
A smaller cost now.
No cost. A coin flip on a breakdown.

d_tender_bid.t: A tender worth bidding for turns up at {n}
d_tender_bid.b: A public body is asking for bids on a large contract. Preparing a good bid takes real effort. You are one of several bidders.

opts.d: A real cost. About 3 in 10 careful bids win.
A smaller cost and a better chance of winning, at a thinner margin.
Nothing changes.

d_customer_credit.t: A large customer asks {n} for credit
d_customer_credit.b: They want 60 days to pay instead of 30. They say they will order more if you agree.

opts.d: Cash is tied up for two months. About 8 in 10 times they pay and order more.
No cash tied up. They may take their business elsewhere.

d_profit_share.t: Staff at {n} ask for a share of profits
d_profit_share.b: A staff representative proposes a profit share. Many teams work harder when they share the win; it also commits you for years.

opts.d: A cost every year when there is a profit. More effort in return.
A smaller commitment.
A coin flip on morale.

d_relocate.b: A larger site on the edge of town costs less. Your regulars may not follow you.

opts.d: Costs a lot to move. About 55% of the time customers follow; otherwise sales drop for months.

later.note: Rent savings at the new site have added up.

opts.d: Nothing changes.

d_hire_star.t: A rival's best person is looking for a move
d_hire_star.b: A top performer at a competitor is open to an offer. They are good, and they will cost more.

opts.d: A higher wage and a recruiting cost. Better quality and speed.
Nothing changes.

d_agency_rebrand.b: A creative agency says a new look would lift sales. Branding results are slow and hard to measure.

opts.d: A big cost. About half the time it lifts awareness and sales.
A small cost and a small effect.
Nothing changes.

d_equipment_upgrade.t: A new machine could speed up {n}
d_equipment_upgrade.b: Newer equipment would raise output and quality. It also means a bigger bill and some teething problems.

opts.d: A big cost. Output and quality rise. Most installations go smoothly, some do not.
A smaller cost, and a smaller gain.
Nothing changes.

d_bank_overdraft.t: The bank offers {n} a bigger credit line
d_bank_overdraft.b: A larger credit line is easy to get. Credit can smooth a slow month, and cost you in interest if you use it as income.

opts.l: Take a small line and use it for stock
opts.d: Cash now, and interest later.

later.note: The credit line was repaid with interest.

opts.d: Nothing changes.

d_price_rise.b: Costs have gone up. You can raise prices a little; some customers will notice and some will leave.

opts.d: More on every sale. About 7 in 10 times customers shrug.
A smaller step.
Nothing changes.

d_free_trial.b: A free first visit or trial often brings new customers, and costs you the visit.

opts.d: Cost of the free visits. Many try it, some stay.
Nothing changes.

d_partner_exit.t: A minority partner of {n} wants to sell
d_partner_exit.b: A partner who owns a small share wants out. You can buy them out, or let them sell to someone else.

opts.d: A big cost. Fewer disagreements and a free hand.

opts.l: Let them sell to an outsider
opts.d: No cost now. The new owner may ask for a say.
Spreads the cost over three instalments.

later.note: The second instalment to the exiting partner was paid.
The final instalment to the exiting partner was paid.

d_lobby.t: An industry body asks {n} to fund lobbying
d_lobby.b: A new rule could raise costs for the whole industry. A lobbying push may soften it, or not.

opts.d: A real cost. About 4 in 10 times the rule is softened.

opts.l: Join but do not fund it
opts.d: A free ride, and a small chance.
A coin flip on whether the rule passes as written.

d_big_contract.t: A large enterprise offers {n} a long contract
d_big_contract.b: A multi-year contract would lift volume. Penalty clauses apply if you miss delivery, and the margin is thin.

opts.d: More volume at a thinner margin. About 8 in 10 times you deliver and nothing goes wrong.

later.note: The contract's delivery review was held.

opts.d: They may agree, or walk away.
No risk, no growth.

d_foundation.b: A company foundation funds local projects and builds goodwill. It costs money every year and pays back slowly.

opts.d: A cost, and a better name in the town.
A smaller cost and effect.
Nothing changes.

d_pension.t: Staff at {n} ask for a better pension
d_pension.b: A better employer pension lifts loyalty and costs money every year.

opts.d: A real cost. Staff stay longer.
People may leave.

d_brand_licence.t: A partner wants to license the brand of {n}
d_brand_licence.b: Another business wants to use your name for its own products. It brings income, and your reputation is on the line.

opts.d: Money now. About 7 in 10 times the partner does it well; otherwise your name suffers.
Less money, and less at stake.
Nothing changes.

d_export_trial.t: A foreign distributor wants the goods of {n}
d_export_trial.b: A distributor abroad wants to carry your products. Shipping and customs cost money, and the first batch is a test.

opts.d: Cash is tied up for months. About half the time orders follow; otherwise you absorb customs and returns.
Nothing changes.

d_buy_customers.t: A retiring competitor sells the customers of {n}'s market
d_buy_customers.b: A retiring owner is selling the customer list and goodwill of a small firm. The customers may or may not stay.

opts.d: A real cost. About 65% of the customers stay.
A lower cost, and they may refuse.
Nothing changes.

d_cost_consultant.t: Consultants promise {n} ten percent lower costs
d_cost_consultant.b: A consulting firm says it can find savings across the company. Their fee is fixed whatever they find.

opts.d: A big fee. About 45% of such projects deliver the saving; others only disrupt the work.
A small cost, a small gain.
Nothing changes.

d_exec_team.t: A headhunter offers {n} a general manager
d_exec_team.b: Hiring a general manager would free you from daily work, and cost a salary every month.

opts.d: A recruiting fee and a long salary. About 65% of the time it goes well.
Nothing changes.

d_data_review.t: A security audit is offered to {n}
d_data_review.b: A security firm offers to test your systems and find weak points. It costs money, and it may find problems you would rather not know about.

opts.d: About 6 in 10 times it finds something worth fixing. Fixing it costs more.
Nothing changes.

d_staff_housing.t: Staff at {n} ask for help with housing
d_staff_housing.b: Rents are high and people are leaving for cheaper cities. A housing allowance costs money and keeps people.

opts.d: A real cost. Fewer people leave.
Some people leave.

d_crisis_pr.t: A news story about {n} is coming
d_crisis_pr.b: A reporter is working on a story about a complaint against your business. You can talk to them, or say nothing.

opts.l: Talk to the reporter and say what happened
opts.d: About 65% of the time the story is fair.
A cost, and a better chance of fair coverage.
A coin flip on how the story reads.
